title: RegisterSession then UnregisterSession lifecycle pair
purpose: Cover encapsulation session establishment and teardown with an explicit runtime session-handle transition instead of a static placeholder-only request.
expected_behavior: The first message should be parsed as a valid RegisterSession request. If the target allocates a session, the harness should substitute the returned nonzero session handle into message 1 in place of ffffffff before sending UnregisterSession. The parser should then accept a normal unregister path.
constraints_preserved: RegisterSession uses command 0x0065 and 4 bytes of payload, matching Length 0x0004.
The RegisterSession payload is conservatively encoded as protocol version 0x0001 and option flags 0x0000, a common EtherNet/IP form inferred from standard behavior.
UnregisterSession uses command 0x0066 with zero payload length.
Both messages use full 24-byte encapsulation headers.
Message 1 contains a deliberate runtime substitution point for the negotiated Session Handle; the literal ffffffff is a placeholder for harness replacement, not a claim of validity if sent unchanged.
issue_safety_notes: Safe stateful coverage only. This sequence does not enter CPF or CIP parsing and is unrelated to the historical malformed ForwardOpen underlength trigger.
